title: Head 3 · Video intake
subtitle: From a clip picked on the phone to a background job that runs ten stages, survives crashes and can be retried.
meta: Built and in use on the Pixel 9 Pro XL.
Picking and copying a video, reading its metadata, the job queue, the worker, the ten stages, crash recovery, retries and the finish notice.

Head 3 · Video intake: from a picked clip to a running job
android/.../video/VideoCapture.kt, VideoMetadata.kt, VideoJobs.kt, VideoWorker.kt, VideoPipeline.kt, ui/screens/VideoScreen.kt

sections.title: Summary
blocks: A person adds a video on the **Video tab**. The app copies it into its own storage, reads when and where it was recorded, and creates one **job**. A background worker then runs the job through ten stages in a fixed order. After each stage the job remembers how far it got, so a crash or restart resumes there instead of starting over. A failing stage is retried up to three times; after that the job is marked failed with its error and a **Retry** button restarts it at the failed stage.
When all ten stages pass, the video is marked **ready** and a notice appears. Only ready videos are searched.

sections.title: Approach

steps: The Video tab opens the Android file picker.
Accepted types: mp4, mov, m4v, avi (the same four the laptop accepts).
The file is streamed into the video's own folder inside the app; the size is counted while copying and the copy stops above **500 MB** with a clear message.
MediaMetadataRetriever reads the recorded time, the duration and GPS when present.
One videos row is written with status processing, and one jobs row with status queued and stage split.

blocks: Copying means the person can move or delete the original afterwards without breaking the memory.

steps: One worker takes the **oldest queued job inside a transaction**, so two workers can never take the same job.
It runs only while there are jobs: no polling when the queue is empty.
The ten stages run in order: split, filter, dedup, scene, small_objects, embed_images, embed_texts, link, latest, finish.
After each stage the job row saves the stage reached. After a crash or restart the job resumes at that stage.
If a stage throws, attempts go up by one and the job returns to the queue. After **3 attempts** it is marked failed, with the error class and the first 200 characters of the message saved.

bullets: The finish stage deletes the picture files of dropped frames (EYKO-59, see Head 4), marks the video ready and shows a notice in the app.
A failed video shows its reason. **Retry** gives the job a fresh set of attempts and restarts it at the failed stage, not from the beginning.
When a new stage is added to the app, videos processed before it are queued again for just the missing stage, so older videos catch up.

rows: The laptop is only a lab (Head 1, decision 5)
Keeps working when the app is closed; not built yet
Simple, testable; stops when Android pauses the app
Start the video again from stage 1
Wastes minutes of model time on long clips
Save the stage reached; resume there
Cheap; one column on the jobs row
Breaks if the person moves or deletes it
Limit 500 MB per video, four container types
Keeps copy time and storage bounded; same types as the laptop
One job per video, stages in a fixed order, stage saved after each
Resumable and easy to reason about; each stage has its own card
3 attempts, then failed with the reason; Retry restarts at the failed stage
Transient errors recover alone; real bugs are shown, not hidden
Half-processed videos would give wrong or missing results
Every video in the memory has the same fields
JVM and on-device tests pass (the phone pipeline suite was 65 of 65 on 15 October; 109 JVM and 104 on-device tests at the 2 November gap review)
Real use: Ego4D clips through the app's own picker
4 clips (27.8 min) processed on the Pixel 9 Pro XL, 20 October
About 1.4 min of processing per minute of video; an 8-minute clip that kept 156 frames took 13.4 min
One 8-minute clip stalled while another app was in front: 21.2 min instead of about 11

bullets: Videos of up to 500 MB go from the gallery into the memory with one tap and no further action.
A crash, a phone restart or a model error does not lose work; the person sees a failed video and its reason, and can retry.
Each video row shows real counts as it moves through the stages.
Processing only runs while the app is alive; Android pauses it in the background (measured stall above).
Copying doubles the storage of each video until the person deletes the original.
Tested on one phone (Pixel 9 Pro XL); the low-end phone has not run the pipeline.
